items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XI, List of Answers on Topics 101:1
items.html: At the time of attaining the Mochin of ZA, the third Tevuna returns to being GAR, and then it too divides into Samekh and Mem, like AVI and Yeshsut. Its first six Sefirot, which are from the Chazeh and above, are called Samekh, and they are in covered Hassadim, like AVI Ilain. And its NHY, which are from the Chazeh and below, are called closed Mem, and they are in revealed Hassadim, like Yeshsut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XI, List of Answers on Topics 101:2
items.html: And you already know that the first six Sefirot of the third Tevuna are called the Mem of Tzelem, and this is because they contain four Mochin: HB, and Hesed and Gevura. For the two Atarin, which are the two halves of Daat, do not couple with one another so as to raise the reflected light up to HB and reveal the Hassadim in the illumination of Hochma, since they have no matter for revealing Hochma, being in the discernment of covered Hassadim, and therefore the two halves of Daat are discerned as two separate Mochin. Hence they are discerned as four Mochin: HB and HG.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XI, List of Answers on Topics 101:3
items.html: But the NHY of the third Tevuna, which are called the Lamed of Tzelem — the discernment of Yeshsut and the closed Mem, whose way is in revealed Hassadim — here the two halves of Daat couple with one another to raise the reflected light up to HB, so as to bring the illumination of Hochma outward and reveal the Hassadim. Thus the two halves of Daat, which are Hesed and Gevura, are found returning to being one Mochin. For they are obliged to couple and join with one another, in order to reveal the illumination of Hochma in the Hassadim, and therefore it is called Lamed, since here there are only three Mochin, namely: Hochma, Bina, Daat, for Hesed and Gevura became one Mochin, as explained (Item 127).
